name: Practice
description: Keeping your own skills sharp: the Pre-mortem (your guess before a diagnosis, and how often you were right), Workshop pieces to do by hand, and your courses as lessons.
agent: Keeping the user's own skills sharp. The Pre-mortem is {state:premortem|on}. When it is on: before you start diagnosing a real problem (a bug, a crash, something slow or broken; not a change the user simply asked for), ask the user one short question with a free answer: what do they think is wrong, and what would they try first? Then work. At the end, compare notes in two or three sentences, then record it with practice_record (kind premortem, with an area and a verdict). The Workshop and the user's courses are in the Practice panel; practice_status shows their record.

intro.tagline: Keeps your own programming skills sharp.
intro.what: When an AI does a lot of the work, your own skills can quietly fade. This has three parts. The Pre-mortem: before Prism fixes a real bug, it asks what you think is wrong, then tells you if you were right, and keeps score. The Workshop: small real pieces of work for you to do by hand. And your C and C++ courses, right here.
helps: You keep making the real decisions, not just watching.
Your score shows where your instincts are strong and where they are slipping.
Your courses are one click away.
intro.example: The app crashes. Before Prism looks, it asks "what do you think is wrong?". You say "the relay". Afterwards it says: close, it was the timeout one layer under it.
